variants.headline: Looking back: bid to remove government fails
variants.sub: The attempt to remove the government by an Assembly vote has failed.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A vote to bring down the government had failed in {colony}.

There are people whose whole interest in this vote is whether it helps them live decently. That is a sensible standard. Labour should keep work, wages and safety in view when assessing the politics, rather than allowing the survival of a ministry to become an end in itself.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We find the conduct of {target} wanting. Whatever the result of this attempt, parliamentary manoeuvre is no substitute for political responsibility or an adequate account of the public interest.

variants.headline: Looking back: confidence challenge falls short
variants.sub: The government has survived a vote intended to bring it down.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: The attempt to remove the government by an Assembly vote had failed.

There are people whose whole interest in this vote is whether it helps them live decently. That is a sensible standard. Labour should keep work, wages and safety in view when assessing the politics, rather than allowing the survival of a ministry to become an end in itself.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We find the conduct of {target} wanting. Whatever the result of this attempt, parliamentary manoeuvre is no substitute for political responsibility or an adequate account of the public interest.

variants.headline: Looking back: government survives the Assembly test
variants.sub: A vote to bring down the government has failed in {colony}.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: The government had survived a vote intended to bring it down.

There are people whose whole interest in this vote is whether it helps them live decently. That is a sensible standard. Labour should keep work, wages and safety in view when assessing the politics, rather than allowing the survival of a ministry to become an end in itself.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We find the conduct of {target} wanting. Whatever the result of this attempt, parliamentary manoeuvre is no substitute for political responsibility or an adequate account of the public interest.
